answer:
**Options that force the sorted (ordered) path without `--sort`:**

- **`--exec` / `--execute` / `-X`** — the ordered path is the only one that knows *which* files matched, so the command runs there (`src/main.zig:2222-2226`; parsing at `src/main.zig:1097-1107`, `src/main.zig:1591-1601`).
- **`--heading`** (aliases `--group-by-file`, and `--pretty`/`-p`, which set `heading`) — streaming emits in completion order, so headers could point at the wrong cluster (`src/main.zig:2227-2231`; parsing at `src/main.zig:1309-1317`, `src/main.zig:1572-1576`).
- **`--pre`** — it also runs per file, so it needs the ordered path (`src/main.zig:2232-2233`; parsing at `src/main.zig:1261-1269`).

Additionally, without any option: **more than one explicit file operand** (all regular files, no directory) forces sorting to match GNU grep argument order (`src/main.zig:2397-2402`).

Inverse: `-k`/`--kamikaze`/`--dataflow` explicitly disables sorting (`src/main.zig:989-991`, `src/main.zig:1642-1644`).
